question: Banda Singh Bahadur, military commander of Khalsa army was executed in:
solution:
The correct answer is__** 1716.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banda Singh Bahadur** was a prominent military commander of the Khalsa army and played a significant role in the early 18th century Sikh history.
 
• He was executed in **1716** by the Mughal authorities after being captured, marking a crucial event in the struggle against Mughal oppression.
 
• His leadership and efforts in establishing Sikh rule in Punjab were pivotal in the fight for Sikh sovereignty.
 
• Banda Singh Bahadur is remembered for his campaigns against **the Mughal Empire **and his attempts to promote social justice and equality.
 
• He is a revered figure in Sikh history, symbolizing resistance against tyranny and the pursuit of justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background**: Banda Singh Bahadur was born as Banda Bahadur in 1670 in the region of Rajouri, now in Jammu and Kashmir, and was a follower of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
 
• **Khalsa Army**: Formed by Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the Khalsa army aimed to defend the rights of the oppressed and promote justice.
 
• **Legacy**: Banda Singh Bahadur established the first Sikh state in Punjab and introduced measures for land reforms, advocating for the rights of peasants and marginalized communities.
 
• **Execution**: His execution was carried out in a brutal manner, intended to serve as a warning to other Sikhs and as a means to suppress the growing Sikh resistance against Mughal rule.
 
• **Commemoration**: Banda Singh Bahadur is commemorated for his sacrifices and contributions to the Sikh community, with various memorials and observances dedicated to his memory.
